metadata.title: 1. Aberrant expression of HERV-K envelope in lymphoma represents an opportunity for novel treatments
metadata.digest_excerpt:
## Top Papers

### 1. Aberrant expression of HERV-K envelope in lymphoma represents an opportunity for novel treatments

Spriano F, Cascione L, Sgrignani J, Bendik N, Zadro A, Napoli S, et al.

*Molecular Cancer Therapeutics*

[10.1158/1535-7163.MCT-25-1542](https://doi.org/10.1158/1535-7163.MCT-25-1542)

HERV-K (HML-2) envelope protein; humanized camelid VHH reformatted as a heavy-chain-only antibody, FF-01.

The scarcest resource in engager design is not a binder but a genuinely tumour-restricted surface antigen, and this paper nominates one: an endogenous retroviral envelope protein re-expressed on the surface of a subset of diffuse large B-cell lymphomas. Locus-level HERV quantification across two independent DLBCL RNA-seq cohorts stratified patients into clinically distinct subgroups tracking an interferon/viral-mimicry programme, surface Env was confirmed by flow cytometry on patient-derived lines, and siRNA knockdown slowed proliferation, so the antigen is not a passenger. The engineering payload is FF-01, a humanized VHH that binds surface Env, drives selective ADCC in primary NK-cell assays, and internalizes rapidly on antigen engagement. That last property cuts both ways: rapid internalization is what an ADC wants, but a CD3 engager needs the antigen to persist at the synapse, so the same arm is not automatically transferable between formats.

DICE score: 4 — Supplies a tumour-restricted surface antigen with human-specific provenance plus a ready humanized single-domain arm, which is the rate-limiting input for new engager programmes rather than an incremental format tweak.

Institute of Oncology Research and IRB Bellinzona, with Robbiani, Cavalli and Bertoni.

paper_text_source: Publisher PDF staged in the private papers repository (emailed-pdf provenance), 23 pages, 56,412 characters of extracted text plus six figure images; Molecular Cancer Therapeutics, doi 10.1158/1535-7163.MCT-25-1542
verification_changes: Nadia stacked four counts in one turn on the detection funnel (eight lines, all eight by qPCR, five of eight by blot, two of eight on the surface); trimmed to eight lines and then five and two, since Theo's next turn says the funnel back.

Nadia called the reporter ADCC signal 'roughly two and a half times baseline' at six hours; Figure 6A shows the Env-positive arm close to 280 per cent of time zero, so the rounding was changed to close to three times.

Nadia attributed the spread in the stromal-cell readout to donors; Figure 6E plots the standard deviation of six biological replicates and the BMSCs were pooled across donors, so it is spread across replicates.
Show notes gave the patient cohort as 342 DLBCLs; the paper states no cohort size, and the figures disagree (342 at risk in the Kaplan-Meier, 345 in the alluvial table), so it now reads about 340.
Show notes rounded the ADCC reporter signal to ~2.5x; corrected to ~2.7x at 6 h to match Figure 6A and the dialogue.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Hi, and welcome to Science TLDR. I'm Nadia.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: And I'm Theo. A target paper today, which I enjoy.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: We do. Molecular Cancer Therapeutics, from the Institute of Oncology Research in Bellinzona: aberrant expression of Herv-K envelope in lymphoma. A retrovirus that entered our ancestors' germline millions of years ago is switched back on in some lymphomas, and its envelope protein reaches the cell surface.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: Okay. Why does that get ten minutes?

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Because the scarce thing in this kind of engineering isn't the binder, it's the antigen. You can raise an arm against almost anything; what you can't manufacture is a protein that sits on tumour cells and nowhere else. These elements are methylated and quiet in healthy tissue, and in cancer that silencing slips.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: So the target would be defined by broken regulation rather than lineage — unlike the antigens we already drug, where hitting C-D-nineteen takes the normal B cells too. How much of this material is in the genome?

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Nearly half of it is transposable elements, and endogenous retroviruses are up to about eight percent. Most of that is invisible in standard analysis: the sequences repeat all over the genome, so the reads multi-map and get discarded. The family here is Herv-K, the subgroup H-M-L-two, which still has intact reading frames.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: Huh — a whole layer routine work throws away. Flag before we go on, though: these envelope genes aren't all junk. Some have real jobs.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Good flag. The syncytins, which let trophoblasts fuse in the placenta, are domesticated retroviral envelope genes. So "it came from a retrovirus" doesn't mean the body treats it as foreign, or that it's absent from normal tissue.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: Noted. What's the central claim?

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Three linked ones, and I'd grade them separately. That Herv-K expression marks real states in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. That the envelope protein is on the surface and the cell needs it. And that an antibody to it can direct killing.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: Start with the patient data.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Two published sequencing cohorts of D-L-B-C-L plus sorted healthy B cells, reprocessed with a tool that assigns those ambiguous reads to specific loci. About three hundred and forty tumours, four clusters, different survival under standard chemo-immunotherapy.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: Which sounds like a new prognostic classifier, and I'd normally be suspicious.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Be suspicious, then give them credit, because they got there first. The clusters track the split everyone already uses, activated B-cell-like versus germinal-centre, and with cell of origin in the model they add nothing independent. They decline to call it a prognostic tool.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: And tumour against normal?

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Many Herv-K elements run higher in tumours, one provirus especially, K-one-one-three. The high expressors also light up interferon signalling — viral mimicry, where the cell sees its own derepressed retroviral transcripts and responds as if infected.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: That's a pathway signature. Not a measurement of protein.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Correct, and that's the hinge. Message is where the patient data stops. Everything about protein on the surface happens in cell lines.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: Give me the cell lines.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Eight D-L-B-C-L lines, three assays. By quantitative P-C-R, the envelope message is detectable in all of them. By immunoblot — total protein in the lysate — five. On the surface, by flow cytometry, two.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: Oh — that's a brutal funnel. Eight, five, two.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: It's the most informative number here, and they draw it as a panel rather than burying it. The attrition isn't mysterious — premature stop codons, and a heavily glycosylated protein whose trafficking decides whether it reaches the membrane. But the therapeutic argument applies only to the last column.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: And of those two, is one doing the heavy lifting?

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Um — yes. Essentially everything functional is one line, which is also the only line carrying the K-one-one-three provirus, on one chromosome.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: Wait. That insertion isn't in everyone's genome?

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: No, it's polymorphic — something like a quarter of people overall, roughly half in African-ancestry cohorts. Other lines make envelope without it, from other family members, and the targeted peptide is conserved across the family. So it isn't one locus — but envelope-positive isn't a clean genotype.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: Second half of that claim — the cell needs it.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Two small interfering R-N-As against separate parts of the transcript. Each knocks the protein down by about half, and proliferation over three days is roughly halved against scrambled control. Viability barely moves, so it's growth, not killing.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: How many replicates behind the knockdown?

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: [thoughtful] Two, and for one guide they disagree with each other quite a bit. In one line. So — consistent with envelope contributing to growth, not a demonstrated dependency. It isn't a passenger; how hard the cell leans on it is untested.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: Now the part I came for. Where does the antibody come from?

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: They modelled the envelope, picked four candidate epitopes on the extracellular portion avoiding glycosylation sites and cysteines, and made them as peptides. Those do double duty. First, serology: a hundred and fifty lymphoma sera screened, and about a third were positive for the best peptide.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: A third. Against what baseline?

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: That's the problem. There's no healthy-donor comparison in the paper, and given what we said about normal tissue, a frequency with no control group can't say whether this is tumour-associated or background. The assay is validated on a dilution series, so it measures something. It has no denominator.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: And the second use of the peptides?

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Selection. A camelid single-domain library — nanobodies — by phage display against those immobilised peptides. Two came out, one held up by surface plasmon resonance. They humanised it onto a human I-g-G-one Fc, so it's heavy-chain-only but still engages Fc receptors. They call it F-F-oh-one.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: Affinity?

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: A dissociation constant of one hundred and forty-two nanomolar. To the peptide.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: To the peptide. Not to envelope on a cell.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Not to envelope on a cell. There's flow binding to positive lines and none to negative lines — the qualitative version — but no affinity against native protein and no copies-per-cell figure. Mid-nanomolar against a fragment is a starting point, not a candidate, and they say as much.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: Is the epitope even reachable on the real thing?

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: They checked, and I liked it. Experimental structures appeared only recently, and they went back and computed solvent accessibility on the single subunit and the assembled trimer. It stays exposed in both.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: So what does the antibody do?

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Nothing alone — no direct anti-tumour activity, reported plainly. The activity is antibody-dependent cytotoxicity: in the reporter assay the envelope-high line gives close to three times baseline at six hours, and the negative line nothing.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: With actual N-K cells?

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Primary N-K cells from healthy donors. In the high expressor, four replicates, all the same direction, and it separates. In the lower expressor, three replicates, and it doesn't clear significance.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: But the text calls that confirmation.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: It does, and that's where the writing gets ahead of the figure. One line killed; one trend in the same direction that didn't reach threshold.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: There's a three-dimensional model too.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: The nicest piece of design here. Lymphoma cells in a fibrin gel with primary N-K cells and bone marrow stromal cells from knee-replacement donors, imaged live for three days. Lymphoma area under the antibody falls to about sixty percent of isotype by day three; the stromal cells are unaffected.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: And they read the stromal cells as the specificity control.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: They call it a strong on-target effect, yes.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: I don't buy it, and it bothers me because the fix is in their own freezer. A stromal cell is a different cell type doing a different thing. The control that settles this is an envelope-negative lymphoma line in the same gel. They have those lines.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Agreed, that's the missing experiment. And the stromal readout is occupied area with wide spread across replicates — blunt, even as the right control.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: The drug-conjugate angle — internalisation.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Taken up by envelope-positive cells, faster and higher than the non-binding nanobody, and in the negative line the ratio goes the other way, below one. Right shape for specificity. But the non-binder internalises substantially too — the separation is about one and a half fold.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: Here's the thing nobody can fix. There's no animal work, and I don't think there could be.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Right. Herv-K is human-specific. No mouse carries this target, so the normal-tissue safety question can't be asked the standard preclinical way. They frame the three-dimensional culture as a replacement-aligned alternative, which is fair, but it answers efficacy, not toxicity.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: And toxicity is the question for a target defined by epigenetic leakage.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Which brings back the syncytins. What decides tumour-restriction is surface staining on primary patient cells and on normal tissue, with this antibody. That doesn't exist yet.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: One disclosure first: the institutes have filed a patent on reagents targeting endogenous retroviruses to kill cancer cells, with several authors as inventors. Declared up front — context, not a reason to doubt the data. Now, two connections, pulling opposite ways. In episode eighty-six, the M-R-one nanobodies had lovely ligand discrimination, but every tumour-killing experiment pulsed the targets with synthetic antigen, because no endogenous ligand had been shown at sufficient density. Here nobody loaded anything.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Which is the harder standard, and they cleared it. The flip side is that density becomes the finding, and the finding is two lines out of eight.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: And that's where the other one bites. Episode eighty-three, the W-T-one peptide-H-L-A antibodies: clean on the biosensor, and on cells half the panel bound a peptide it shouldn't have. Specificity failures don't show up in the purified assay. They show up on cells.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Hmm. And there's no counter-screen of that kind here. Binding to negative lines is the only negative evidence — a handful of lymphoma lines, not a proteome, not normal tissue. So the specificity claim is untested rather than contradicted, but untested where it caught the earlier one out.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: Alright. Three takeaways. First: quantifying endogenous retroviruses at individual loci, from reads routine pipelines discard, reconstructs the known subtypes of this lymphoma — real signal, and not sold as a prognostic tool.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: Second: envelope is detectable by message in all eight cell lines, by blot in five, on the surface in two — and every functional result rests on one of those two, which is also the only line carrying that polymorphic provirus.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: Third: the antibody is a real proof of principle — N-K killing in two and three dimensions, and internalisation — but selected and measured against a peptide at mid-nanomolar affinity, with no envelope-negative lymphoma control in the three-dimensional assay.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: So I'd believe the antigen is on some lymphoma cells and does something for them. I wouldn't yet believe it's tumour-restricted.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Same here.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: What would change your mind?

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Surface staining on primary patient tumour cells, with copies per cell, against normal human tissue in the same assay. If it's on patient cells and absent elsewhere, this becomes a programme.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: Mine's cheaper. Put an envelope-negative lymphoma line in that fibrin gel, same N-K cells, same antibody. If the negative line dies too, nothing upstream matters.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: That would settle a lot. So: Molecular Cancer Therapeutics, D-O-I ten dot one one five eight slash one five three five dash seven one six three dot M-C-T dash two five dash one five four two. Thanks for listening.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: See you next time.
